cues.text: Good morning everyone. My name’s Joy Parkins and I’m the restaurant manager.
I understand that none of you have had any previous experience as kitchen assistants, but
most of our kitchen assistants say they enjoy the work.
They like the fact that they have so many different things to do, which means they never
get bored.
You’ve all shown up on time, which is an excellent start.
You need to be careful because the floors can get very wet and slippery.
Those of you with long hair have got it well out of the way, but some of you will need to
remove your rings and bracelets and remember to leave them at home tomorrow, as they can
be a safety hazard.
It’s going to be a busy day today.
We don’t have any tables free for this evening, and only a few for lunch.
Fortunately the Head Chef is back, because he was away on holiday all last week, which
meant the other chefs had extra work.
There’s some equipment you mustn’t use until you’ve been properly trained, like the waste
disposal system.
Then for the two of you who are under 18, the meat slicer is out of bounds.
None of you are allowed to use the electric mixer until you’ve been shown how it works.
This can be a stressful job.
You’ll be working an eight-hour day for the first week, though you can do overtime after
that if you want to. However long the hours are, you’ll get a break in the middle.
What you will find is that you’re on your feet all day long, lifting and carrying, and
when someone tells you to do something you need to do it straightaway.
Now let me tell you about some of the people you need to know.
I’m Joy Parkins and I decide who does what during the day and how long they work for.
One person whose name you must remember is David Field.
If you injure yourself at all, even if it’s really minor, you must report to him and
he’ll make sure the incident is recorded and you get the appropriate treatment.
Then there’s Dexter Wills.
He’s the person you need to see if you smash a plate or something like that.
Don’t just leave it and hope no one will notice. Finally, there’s Mike Smith.
He’s the member of staff who takes care of all the stores of perishables, so if you
notice we’re getting low in flour or sugar or something, make sure you let him know so he
can put in an order.
